section_about:
The Accounting team owns the numbers at a rapidly scaling startup.
We ensure accurate, timely financial reporting in accordance with U.S.
GAAP while designing scalable processes and strong controls that support expansion across teams and geographies.
Partnering closely with Sales, People, Legal, and Operations, we drive thoughtful spend management, contract oversight, and operational excellence, balancing precision with agility in a fast-moving environment where our work directly enables the company's next stage of growth.
We're looking for a technically strong Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting Manager to own complex, non-routine accounting matters as Decagon scales.
This is a high-impact individual contributor role for someone who thrives on solving thorny GAAP questions, revenue recognition, business combinations, and stock-based compensation among them, and can turn them into clear, well-documented conclusions the business can act on.
You'll partner closely with Legal, Sales, Founders Office, Revenue Operations, and Finance to help dictate and guide deal structure and pricing strategy before new products and deals go to market while helping build the technical accounting infrastructure, policies, memos, and controls that a fast-growing, pre-IPO company needs.
section_responsibilities:
- Own technical accounting positions under U.S.
GAAP for complex transactions, including revenue recognition (ASC 606), business combinations (ASC 805), and stock-based compensation (ASC 718), with audit-ready memos behind every conclusion
- Review non-standard customer contracts with Legal, Sales, Founders Office, Revenue Operations, and Finance, and get the revenue treatment right on new products and pricing before they are rolled out
- Own equity and stock-based compensation accounting, including 409A and award valuations with external specialists, plus M&A and financing activity as it comes up
- Build Decagon's technical accounting policies from the ground up that hold up as we scale
- Drive conclusions with external auditors and technical consultants, and raise the rigor of external reporting as we approach IPO readiness
- Track new accounting standards and tell leadership what they mean for us, in plain terms
- Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent designation preferred
- 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including a combination of Big 4/public accounting and industry experience at a high-growth technology or SaaS company
- Deep, hands-on technical accounting expertise in ASC 606, 805 and 718, with demonstrated experience drafting memos on complex, non-routine transactions
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical accounting conclusions for non-finance stakeholders
- A self-starter who's comfortable owning ambiguous, high-stakes problems independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
Even better if you have
- Experience with lease accounting (ASC 842), capitalized software (ASC 350-40), or debt and equity instruments (ASC 480)
- Familiarity with ERP and financial reporting tools
- Experience using AI and automation tools to accelerate technical accounting research, memo drafting, or audit support

Decagon builds mission-critical AI products that impact millions of users and directly drive our customers' success.
Our New York engineering teams build products and foundational systems across customer support, growth and new verticals.

Your team's primary responsibility is to build reusable products and systems.
You'll stay close to users and customers to inform product decisions, while partnering with product and design to deliver solutions that scale.
Managers here are expected to operate with high ownership and technical depth while helping their teams move quickly and maintain a high quality bar.
This role is for someone who enjoys mentoring engineers, exercising product judgment and diving deep into complex technical challenges.

- Enterprise Data Lifecycle: Build the critical systems behind our enterprise data privacy and retention commitments.

- Collections: Build our product for the debt collection vertical, partnering with external design partners to discover user needs, iterate on the product and prove its value in a new market.
- Proactive Agents: Build our outbound, proactive agent product.

Each one puts a Decagon agent in front of millions of users, fielding hundreds of millions of conversations a year.

Data Lifecycle at Decagon builds the systems that govern how sensitive customer data is handled throughout its lifetime: what we store, who can access it, how we redact it, and when we delete it.
We turn complex privacy requirements into reliable infrastructure and product that customers can configure and trust.
Our AI agents work with sensitive information across conversations, tool calls, and customer systems.
The frameworks we build need to protect that data consistently across the platform, while preserving the context customers need to operate and improve their agents.
A failure mode we debug in production becomes a guardrail, a test, or a piece of tooling that catches it everywhere.
Our systems run for companies like Hertz, American Airlines, and Notion across chat, voice, email, and SMS.
You'll design and build the platform infrastructure that let customers control how their data is collected, retained, redacted, and deleted.
That means strong engineering underneath, and clear abstractions on top that hold up across different enterprise requirements without forking per customer.
You'll work day to day with product management, governance, and security: understanding customer requirements, defining data handling guarantees, reviewing designs, and iterating through launch.
You'll stay close enough to customers to understand their privacy and operational needs in depth and to ensure what you're building is actually right for them.
On this team, that includes verifying that sensitive data is protected and the action actually completes.
An understanding of durable and fault-tolerant systems is key.

- Handle data lifecycle systems at scale, including backfills, partial failures, and safe rollouts; your work will touch critical flows for Fortune 100 companies

The Security Engineering team at Decagon protects the platform that powers the most advanced conversational AI agents for enterprise customers across voice, chat, email and SMS.
We build the security foundations that enable Decagon's AI agents to handle sensitive customer data with trust while defending against sophisticated, AI-enabled threats at massive scale.
Our mission is to provide magical support experiences - ensuring that AI agents and human agents can collaborate safely to help users resolve their issues while maintaining the highest standards of security and privacy.
Lead the application security strategy and implementation for Decagon AI's conversational platform that serves enterprise customers at scale.

You own how performance is defined, measured, and demonstrated against these criteria, from translating them into metrics we operationalize and deliver, to improving the ones that are key to each evaluation.
You hold that from the first pre-sales evaluation through the life of the account.
Our team sits within Agent Product Management and focuses mostly on our largest and most complex deployments, while supporting the data needs of Decagon customers more broadly.
We are small relative to that surface area, which means the scope you own is very wide and exceptionally cross-functional.
The work compounds accordingly: every metric you define on a flagship deployment becomes the default for the deals that follow, and the frameworks you build outlive any single account.
Demonstrating the value of our product is everyone's responsibility, not only ours.

That is what lets us stay focused on the hardest and most novel measurement problems our customers bring us, which gives this team real influence over the long-term product roadmap.
Most of your time will be spent working directly with customers to establish what should be measured and then building what produces it.
Usually, the hard part comes from driving alignment, not the analysis itself.
You own both reporting on performance and improving it, working alongside the Agent Product Managers, Agent Strategy Managers, Strategic Account Directors, and Agent Deployment Engineers on each account.

The Agent Platform team builds the runtime and model orchestration layer that powers Decagon's agents in production.
At the core of this work is the agent harness: the routing, execution logic, tool orchestration, and control-plane systems that determine how an agent behaves in a live conversation.

Our research shows that an agent's task execution reliability increasingly depends on the orchestration layer that wraps around it.
This is highly experimental, frontier-style engineering.
The team continuously analyzes real-world failures, builds feedback loops through offline evaluation and online experimentation, and iterates quickly to improve quality, reliability, and capability.
As model capabilities evolve, the team regularly rethinks system design to push agent performance forward in production.

You will own complex, distributed systems that sit at the heart of the agent runtime: execution frameworks, model orchestration logic, and experimentation platforms that ensure agents are fast, reliable, and continuously improving.
Your work will directly impact how agents reason, take actions, and deliver outcomes across millions of interactions.
This role operates in a fast-moving, ambiguous space with tight feedback loops.
You'll move fluidly between diagnosing production issues, designing new system abstractions, and running experiments to improve agent behavior.
You'll collaborate closely with Research, Infra, and Product teams to ship improvements safely and at scale.

section_about:
The Agent Platform team builds the runtime and model orchestration layer that powers Decagon's agents in production.
At the core of this work is the agent harness: the routing, execution logic, tool orchestration, and control-plane systems that determine how an agent behaves in a live conversation.
The team owns the full execution lifecycle of each conversation-from selecting workflows and orchestrating multiple models (e.g., router/planner/supervisor patterns), to coordinating tool calls, enforcing safety constraints, and communicating back to the user.
The team operates across both real-time systems (e.g., voice interactions with strict latency requirements) and longer-horizon execution (supporting more complex reasoning and workflows).
Our research shows that an agent's task execution reliability increasingly depends on the orchestration layer that wraps around it.
This is highly experimental, frontier-style engineering.
The team continuously analyzes real-world failures, builds feedback loops through offline evaluation and online experimentation, and iterates quickly to improve quality, reliability, and capability.
As model capabilities evolve, the team regularly rethinks system design to push agent performance forward in production.
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Agent Platform team, you will design and build the systems that govern how Decagon agents operate in real-world environments.
You will own complex, distributed systems that sit at the heart of the agent runtime: execution frameworks, model orchestration logic, and experimentation platforms that ensure agents are fast, reliable, and continuously improving.
Your work will directly impact how agents reason, take actions, and deliver outcomes across millions of interactions.
This role operates in a fast-moving, ambiguous space with tight feedback loops.
You'll move fluidly between diagnosing production issues, designing new system abstractions, and running experiments to improve agent behavior.
You'll collaborate closely with Research, Infra, and Product teams to ship improvements safely and at scale.

The Infrastructure team builds and operates the foundations that power Decagon: networking, data, ML serving, developer platform, and real‐time voice.
We partner closely with product, data, and ML to deliver high‐scale, low‐latency systems with clear SLOs and great developer ergonomics.

Decagon builds agentic AI that resolves customer support conversations end to end, for companies ranging from fast-growing startups to some of the largest financial institutions in the world.
Keeping that system fast, reliable, and secure (across our multi-tenant cloud and inside customers' own locked-down environments) is an infrastructure problem, and that's the problem this role owns.
You'll build the platforms and abstractions our product teams ship on, and you'll architect and operate the deployments that run our agents inside enterprise customer clouds, where security, compliance, and operational rigor matter as much as speed.
The work is core infrastructure at heart: reliability, CI/CD, deployment automation, on-call.
You'll be joining a team with real infrastructure and momentum already in place, but there's no established playbook for running agentic systems at this scale, so a big part of the job is figuring it out as the technology shifts and usage grows by orders of magnitude.

- Keep agentic workloads reliable

Decagon is seeking a Senior Commercial Counsel to join our dedicated, collaborative and fast-growing team.
This is a remote role for those based outside of San Francisco and New York.
This role will serve as a senior strategic legal partner to the business, with primary responsibility for leading some of the company's most complex, high-impact, revenue-generating transactions and partnering closely with sales leadership and other senior stakeholders to structure, negotiate and close sophisticated enterprise SaaS, on-premises and strategic commercial agreements.
This role will also support broader commercial legal initiatives, including advising on strategic go-to-market models, channel programs, privacy and regulatory matters, commercial policies, maintaining and improving commercial legal templates and playbooks and partnering with cross-functional stakeholders on strategic business initiatives.
The successful candidate will be a creative and analytical thinker with exceptional business judgment who is highly detail-oriented and embraces a pragmatic, business-first approach to legal counseling.
They will possess the strategic thinking, executive presence and interpersonal skills necessary to build trusted advisor relationships across the organization while remaining approachable, collaborative and solutions oriented.
The successful candidate also brings significant experience leading negotiations of complex, high-value commercial agreements with Fortune 500 and other sophisticated enterprise customers, frequently negotiating on customer paper and within highly regulated industries such as healthcare, financial services and the public sector.
They are comfortable navigating novel legal and commercial issues, balancing risk with business objectives and partnering cross-functionally to help drive strategic outcomes.
This individual is an exceptional drafter and strategic negotiator, who can quickly distinguish material legal risk from negotiable issues and develop practical solutions that keep transactions moving toward successful execution.
They have a proven track record of serving as a trusted advisor to business leaders, successfully managing sophisticated counterparties and mentoring attorneys while helping elevate the overall capabilities of the commercial legal team.
